paragraphs.text: •Artificial Intelligence (AI) accelerators, microprocessors (CPUs) for servers, graphics processing units (GPUs), accelerated processing units (APUs), data processing units (DPUs), AI Network Interface Cards (AI NICs), Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs) and adaptive System-on-Chip (SoC) products for data centers;

Net revenue for the three months ended September 26, 2026 was $13.4 billion, a 45% increase compared to the prior year period. The increase in net revenue was driven by an increase in Data Center segment revenue primarily driven by the strong demand for our AMD EPYC™ processors and the launch of our AMD Instinct™ MI450 Series GPUs, and an increase in Embedded segment revenue as demand strengthened across end markets, partially offset by a decrease in our Client and Gaming segment revenue primarily due to lower demand for semi-custom products.

Gross margin for the three months ended September 26, 2026 was 54% compared to gross margin of 52% for the prior year period, a 2 percentage point increase primarily driven by a favorable product mix, including higher Data Center segment revenue.

Operating income for the three months ended September 26, 2026 was $2.8 billion compared to operating income of $1.3 billion for the prior year period. The increase in operating income was due to higher gross profit, partially offset by higher operating expenses. Net income for the three months ended September 26, 2026 was $2.4 billion compared to net income of $1.2 billion for the prior year period. The increase in net income was primarily driven by higher operating income.

As of September 26, 2026, our cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments were $15.8 billion compared to $10.6 billion as of December 27, 2025. During the nine months ended September 26, 2026, we generated $6.5 billion of cash from operating activities and we returned $221 million to stockholders through the repurchase of common stock under our stock repurchase program (Repurchase Program).

In August and September 2026, we entered into definitive agreements to acquire Taalas Inc. and World Labs Technologies, Inc. to strengthen our model research and inference capabilities and development of future super intelligence (SI) hardware, software and systems. The acquisitions are expected to close in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2026, subject to regulatory approvals and customary closing conditions.

paragraphs.sub: Results of Continuing Operations › Data Center
paragraphs.text: Data Center net revenue of $8.5 billion for the three months ended September 26, 2026 increased by 97%, compared to net revenue of $4.3 billion for the prior year period. Data Center net revenue of $21.0 billion for the nine months ended September 26, 2026 increased by 87%, compared to net revenue of $11.3 billion for the prior year period. The increase in both periods was primarily driven by strong demand for our AMD EPYC processors and AMD Instinct GPUs.

paragraphs.sub: Results of Continuing Operations › Data Center
paragraphs.text: Data Center operating income was $2.9 billion for the three months ended September 26, 2026, compared to operating income of $1.1 billion for the prior year period. Data Center operating income was $6.6 billion for the nine months ended September 26, 2026, compared to operating income of $1.9 billion for the prior year period. The increase in operating income in both periods was primarily driven by higher revenue, partially offset by higher cost of sales and operating expenses.

paragraphs.sub: Results of Continuing Operations › Client and Gaming
paragraphs.text: Client and Gaming net revenue of $3.7 billion for the three months ended September 26, 2026 decreased by 8%, compared to net revenue of $4.0 billion for the prior year period. Client and Gaming net revenue of $11.2 billion for the nine months ended September 26, 2026 increased by 5%, compared to net revenue of $10.6 billion for the prior year period.

paragraphs.sub: Results of Continuing Operations › Client and Gaming
paragraphs.text: Gaming net revenue of $0.8 billion for the three months ended September 26, 2026 decreased by 40% compared to net revenue of $1.3 billion for the prior year period. Gaming net revenue of $2.3 billion for the nine months ended September 26, 2026 decreased by 26% compared to net revenue of $3.1 billion for the prior year period. The decrease in both periods was primarily due to lower semi-custom revenue.

Embedded net revenue of $1.1 billion for the three months ended September 26, 2026 increased by 29%, compared to net revenue of $857 million for the prior year period. Embedded net revenue of $3.0 billion for the nine months ended September 26, 2026 increased by 18%, compared to net revenue of $2.5 billion for the prior year period. Net revenue increased in both periods as demand strengthened across end markets.

paragraphs.sub: Results of Continuing Operations › International Sales
paragraphs.text: International sales, based on billing location of customers who purchased directly from us, were 57% and 64% of net revenue for the three months ended September 26, 2026 and September 27, 2025, respectively, and 66% and 67% of net revenue for the nine months ended September 26, 2026 and September 27, 2025, respectively. We expect that international sales will continue to be a significant portion of total sales in the foreseeable future. Substantially all of our sales transactions were denominated in U.S. dollars.

paragraphs.sub: Gross Margin and Expenses › Gross Margin
paragraphs.text: Gross margin was 54% and 52% for the three months ended September 26, 2026 and September 27, 2025, respectively, where the increase was driven by a favorable product mix, including higher Data Center segment revenue. Gross margin was 54% and 47% for the nine months ended September 26, 2026 and September 27, 2025, respectively, where the increase was driven by the absence of inventory and related charges associated with the U.S. government export control on AMD Instinct MI308 Data Center GPU products that was recorded in the prior year period and a favorable product mix, including higher Data Center segment revenue.

In addition to our debt obligations, we have entered and may continue to enter into commercial arrangements to support our operations and anticipated growth as well as the development of the broader SI infrastructure ecosystem by our customers and commercial partners and expand access to our AI technologies. These arrangements include long-term capacity purchase agreements, cloud compute capacity commitments, leases (including leases for general corporate purposes and data center leases), lease guarantees and other credit support and financing arrangements.
